issue.title: FW tools logging system is broken

failure.body:
**Description**
FW tools logging system has been broken by recent changes, when `sonic-py-common` package has been introduced.
The issue is caused by logger implementation which has several weak places:
1. It implicitly suppress logging messages up to `NOTICE` level: [logger.py](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/src/sonic-py-common/sonic_py_common/logger.py#L34)
The side effect is seen due to Mellanox Platform API implementation: [chassis.py](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/platform/mellanox/mlnx-platform-api/sonic_platform/chassis.py#L15)
2. It is not flexible enough: there is no way to configure `logoption`

FW tools update for `Azure/sonic-utilities` [master](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-utilities/commit/621aad0151b6a64ab5c64e81f73f93b2c6b827bd#diff-dfdf5772988b97db10b1fe0354cbbe81a91f14939a9ba68091e5038990f50a13)/[201911](https://github.com/Azure/sonic-utilities/commit/d05f354ea1e5295afe3c9726bacabcf2154e430c#diff-dfdf5772988b97db10b1fe0354cbbe81a91f14939a9ba68091e5038990f50a13) is not consistent: basically logger modifications is missing for `201911`

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Initiate firmware update
```
root@sonic:/home/admin# fwutil install chassis component CPLD1 fw /tmp/cpld_burn.vme -y
Warning: Power cycle (with 30 sec delay) or refresh image is required to complete CPLD1 firmware update.
Installing firmware:
    /tmp/cpld_burn.vme
```

**Describe the results you received:**
```
root@sonic:/home/admin# tail -F /var/log/syslog | grep fwutil
```

**Describe the results you expected:**
```
root@sonic:/home/admin# tail -F /var/log/syslog | grep fwutil
Oct 21 <IPV6>.107183 sonic INFO fwutil: Firmware install started: component=MSN3700C/CPLD1, firmware=/tmp/cpld_burn.vme
Oct 21 <IPV6>.107527 sonic INFO fwutil: Firmware install ended: component=MSN3700C/CPLD1, firmware=/tmp/cpld_burn.vme, status=success
```

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**
Logging is suppressed:
```
Oct 21 <IPV6>.030912 sonic ERR fwutil: => error
Oct 21 <IPV6>.031530 sonic WARNING fwutil: => warning
Oct 21 <IPV6>.031952 sonic NOTICE fwutil: => notice
```
Logging is restored:
```
Oct 21 <IPV6>.095809 sonic INFO fwutil: Chassis loaded successfully
Oct 21 <IPV6>.105335 sonic ERR fwutil: => error
Oct 21 <IPV6>.105777 sonic WARNING fwutil: => warning
Oct 21 <IPV6>.106136 sonic INFO fwutil: => info
Oct 21 <IPV6>.106487 sonic NOTICE fwutil: => notice
Oct 21 <IPV6>.106832 sonic DEBUG fwutil: => debug
Oct 21 <IPV6>.107183 sonic INFO fwutil: Firmware install started: component=MSN3700C/CPLD1, firmware=/tmp/cpld_burn.vme
Oct 21 <IPV6>.107527 sonic INFO fwutil: Firmware install ended: component=MSN3700C/CPLD1, firmware=/tmp/cpld_burn.vme, status=success
```

resolution.title: [sonic-py-common]: Fix syslog implicit min priority override
resolution.description:
Signed-off-by: Nazarii Hnydyn <<EMAIL>>

Current implementation of logger class is based on standard python syslog library.
Thus, logger class can be instantiated in different places and share the same context across the entire process.
This means that reducing log severity level will affect other modules which use logging facility.

**- Why I did it**
* To fix syslog implicit min priority override

**- How I did it**
* Added per instance log severity check

**- How to verify it**
1. Run code snippet
```
from sonic_py_common import logger

log1 = logger.Logger(log_identifier='myApp1')
log1.set_min_log_priority_debug()
log1.log_error("=> this is error")
log1.log_warning("=> this is warning")
log1.log_notice("=> this is notice")
log1.log_info("=> this is info")
log1.log_debug("=> this is debug")

log2 = logger.Logger(
    log_identifier='myApp2',
    log_facility=logger.Logger.LOG_FACILITY_DAEMON,
    log_option=(logger.Logger.LOG_OPTION_NDELAY | logger.Logger.LOG_OPTION_PID)
)
log2.log_error("=> this is error")
log2.log_warning("=> this is warning")
log2.log_notice("=> this is notice")
log2.log_info("=> this is info")
log2.log_debug("=> this is debug")
```
2. Sample output:
```
Oct 23 <IPV6>.447301 sonic ERR myApp1: => this is error
Oct 23 <IPV6>.447908 sonic WARNING myApp1: => this is warning
Oct 23 <IPV6>.448305 sonic NOTICE myApp1: => this is notice
Oct 23 <IPV6>.448696 sonic INFO myApp1: => this is info
Oct 23 <IPV6>.449063 sonic DEBUG myApp1: => this is debug

Oct 23 <IPV6>.449442 sonic ERR myApp2[19178]: => this is error
Oct 23 <IPV6>.449819 sonic WARNING myApp2[19178]: => this is warning
Oct 23 <IPV6>.450183 sonic NOTICE myApp2[19178]: => this is notice
```
